title: Youth programs whose day counts are mostly young people counted in aggregate
question: Which programs report more participant days than their counted participants could attend, and how much of the department's published totals do they make?
finding: In 2025-26, 13 programs reported more participant days than their individually counted participants could have attended on every service date; together 569,646 of the department's 2,620,482 days (22%), against 624,706 of 2,712,571 (23%) in 2024-25. The largest is Playworks Education Energized - Playworks San Francisco Safe and Healthy Play: 479,298 days from 181 participants on 193 dates, 18% of all the department's days and 55% of its service area's, on $303,000. Without it the service area's spending per participant day is $45.25, not $20.74.
how: For each program page: participant days (the Activities table) against participants times service dates. More days than that product can only come from young people the program reports in aggregate, which the page footnote says are included.
limits: Aggregate counting is what some grants ask for (recess and school-wide programs, outreach events); the counts may be honest. The question is what a published total of days, or a cost per day, measures when one program supplies a fifth of it. The pages give no counting method.
